newsitem.title: USA: Allied Deals wins bulk of aluminum bid - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Allied Deals wins bulk of aluminum bid - dealers.

text.p: Allied Deals is expected to win the bulk of the latest offering of aluminum by the U.S. Defense National Stockpile Center, said several dealers familiar with the situation.
Allied bid on 8,000 short tons with prices ranging between $1,597.60 a short ton (79.88 cents a lb) and $1,612.60 a ton (80.63 cents a lb). The stockpile is believed to be offering 10,050 tons.
The London Metal Exchange settlement price was 78.15 cents Wednesday, when the bids were opened.
Alcan Aluminum, which bid $1,610.02 a ton (80.50 cents a lb) for 500 tons.
VAW of America, which bid $1,608 a ton (80.40 cents a lb) for 300 tons.
Reynolds Metals, which bid, $1,607 a ton (80.35 cents a lb) for 500 tons.
Alcoa, which bid $1,604 a ton (80.20 cents a lb) for 250 tons.
Global Minerals & Metals, which bid $1,599.15 a ton (79.96 cents a lb) for 500 tons.

"The fact is that if you take Allied Deals out of the picture, the bids were pretty conservative overall," one bidder said. "The larger bids (that didn't win) were down in the 60's and lower 70's. You had several large players that didn't even bid."
Conspicuous in their absence were Mitsui, MG Metals and Billiton Stratcor.
Traders suspected that the weakening premiums as a result of the widening backwardation on the LME was discourging bidders.
"People are very cautious because of the impact the backwardation is having on premiums," said one.
Premiums typically fall in a backwardation because there is a disincentive to carry metal when the future price is at a discount to the cash price.

The LME cash-to-three-month backwardation was $4/$8 at 1315 EDT. Spot premiums range between 3.75-5.00 cents over LME cash, with the most of the volume at 4.25-4.50 cents. Last week premiums were 4.00-5.00 cents.
The stockpile is expected to formally announce the bidders soon.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
